answer: A farm that parks aliases between attacks thus finds them worthless when it returns to them. The cipher decay curve is applied at each close, vine records the drop, and spiral recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 2 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. Repeating the trick 58 times costs 9 separate deposits and 10 separate proofs of work. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
